priority.rationale: New users and members need a useful workspace and a safe way to present themselves to the website community.

execution.objective: Specify a role-aware User and Member Workspace that reuses the established Member Dashboard experience, enables consent-based public profile display in website communities, and preserves the canonical invitation path for user-to-member conversion.
success_criteria: A regular user has a useful dashboard with profile controls and learning entry points.
A member retains existing member dashboard capabilities and sees member-only features only when canonically authorized.
The shared workspace experience is based on the established MemberHub design; the primitive /hub/member page is not the design baseline.
The dashboard and server enforce user/member capability boundaries; hiding a control in the UI alone is insufficient.
A user can preview a public profile and explicitly choose whether to publish it.
A profile is private until its owner opts into publication.
The public profile projection contains only approved profile fields; private contact details are excluded unless their existing visibility settings permit disclosure.
Community cards and discovery consume the canonical profile projection and enforce visibility rules without duplicating identity data.
A user who accepts a member invitation follows APP-INV-001, keeps the same authenticated identity, and receives member capabilities only after canonical invitation acceptance.
No new identity, membership, invitation, or contact-visibility authority is created.
English, Vietnamese, and Chinese are supported for the user/member workspace entry and public-profile controls.
Founder runtime review verifies user and member access boundaries, profile visibility, community display, and invitation-based conversion.
Notification outcomes are visible and recoverable: delivery failures do not grant membership, lose invitation state, or create duplicate identities or invitations.
Notification content and recipient selection respect account state, invitation authority, privacy settings, and approved contact data.
The implementation reuses existing Resend integration, notification preferences, templates, and delivery records where available; it creates no parallel notification authority.

After admin email-template and notification management is completed and runtime-verified, required transactional messages for signup confirmation, invitation delivery/receipt, invitation acceptance, and canonical user-to-member transition use the approved existing notification pipeline.
Required onboarding and security messages remain system-managed and available regardless of a user's subscription or credit balance.
Delivery failures are visible and recoverable; they do not grant membership, lose invitation state, or create duplicate identities or invitations.

Premium notification campaigns or user-configurable paid notification services are not enabled by this WCS; a later WCS must define subscription/credit entitlements, consent, preferences, quotas, and delivery controls.

portfolio_binding.sequencing_note: The GE/SLL chain is a separate stream and does not block this work. Within this WCS, stabilize the role/visibility contract first; then build the shared dashboard and public-profile projection; then integrate community discovery and verify invitation-based role conversion.

user_workspace: Invitation receipt and a clear path to accept a member invitation
member_workspace: Existing member dashboard presentation and capabilities
Member-only invitations, relationships, membership, and credits, subject to canonical authorization
The same profile preview and visibility controls available to users

public_profile.publication: Explicit owner opt-in after preview; private by default.
public_profile.projection: Use the canonical profile source and existing visibility registry.
public_profile.community_display: Community cards and discovery show only published, visibility-permitted fields.
public_profile.private_contact_rule: Do not expose private email, phone, or contact channels in public responses.

user_to_member_transition.identity_rule: Keep the same authenticated user identity; do not create a duplicate account.
user_to_member_transition.entitlement_rule: Grant member-only capabilities only after canonical membership is established.

privacy_and_authority: Enforce visibility on server responses as well as in the interface.
Do not create a second profile, identity, membership, or invitation authority.
Do not silently publish a profile or expose unselected contact details.

prerequisites: Complete and runtime-verify admin email-template and notification management under its identified active WCS/authority.
Verify GE-RMP-014 Resend transport and GEX-NOTIFY-001 notification pipeline contracts and current production status.
onboarding_transactional_events: User signup confirmation and relevant account status
Invitation acceptance and canonical member activation
User-to-member transition using the same authenticated identity
transactional_rules: Use the approved existing notification service, templates, preferences, and delivery records.
Keep necessary onboarding and security messages system-managed and independent of subscription or credit balance.
Email delivery or failure never grants membership; APP-INV-001 remains the authority for invitation acceptance.
Do not disclose private profile or contact details in notification content.

future_requirements: Quotas, usage records, and billing/credit deduction behavior
Admin controls, abuse prevention, and delivery failure handling

forbidden_surface: Runtime implementation before a separate implementation authority is approved
Unauthorised exposure of private profile or contact data
Granting member-only privileges to regular users

founder_runtime_test.test_definition: After implementation authority is approved and runtime is built, verify regular-user and member dashboards, public-profile opt-in and visibility, community display, and user-to-member invitation acceptance.
founder_runtime_test.expected_outcome: Users receive learning-oriented workspace access without member-only privileges; members retain authorized features; public profile data respects owner consent and visibility; invitation acceptance upgrades the same identity through the canonical path.
